raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`update_weights_from_tensor` indexes `serialized_named_tensors` by `tp_rank`, so an HTTP caller has to send one identical copy of the payload per rank. For a trainer that pushes a LoRA adapter to external engines over HTTP every step, that multiplies the request by the engine's TP size (base64 inside JSON on top), and rank 0 also forwards the whole request to the other ranks.

Measured with miles' http-lora transport (radixark/miles#3690) on GLM-5.3 744B with the GLM LoRA cookbook's full MoE LoRA (4.1 GB adapter), rollouts on MI355X, trainer on B300:

| rollout engines | copies per request | sync per step |
|---|---|---|
| 2 engines × TP4 | 4 | 409 s |
| 1 engine × TP8 (dp-attention) | 8 | > 600 s (hit the 600 s weight-update timeout) |
| 1 engine × TP8 (dp-attention), this PR + miles sending one copy | 1 | **127 s** (103 s of it the POST) |
| 1 engine × TP8, this PR + miles sending one copy | 1 | **84 s** |

The per-rank copies are only needed for CUDA-IPC payloads (the in-process `Engine` path), where a rank must not open another rank's handles. HTTP callers ship plain CPU tensors, which carry no handles.

## Modifications

- `BaseTpWorker.deserialize_own_rank`: with a single entry, every rank deserializes entry 0; a per-rank list is indexed by `tp_rank` as before.
- Backward compatible: per-rank lists behave exactly as today, and a single entry on a multi-rank engine used to raise `IndexError`, so no working caller changes behaviour. In-process callers (`Engine._serialize_tensors_per_rank`, CUDA-IPC) keep sending per-rank lists.

Source: 1 file, +5/-4.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_tp_worker_shared_tensor_payload.py`: 2 cases (per-rank list reads its own entry on ranks 0-3; a single shared entry is read by ranks 0-3). Fails without the change on the shared case, passes with it. `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_weight_update_tensor_rank.py` still passes, in either order.
- End to end: GLM-5.3 744B LoRA, miles fully-async with http-lora tensors mode sending one copy per engine, one TP8 engine on 8× MI355X: the 4.1 GB adapter syncs in 84 s every step (v0-v2: 84.2 / 84.1 / 84.9 s) and the engine serves it; trainer vs rollout log-prob diff 0.036 → 0.033, KL 5.4e-3 → 4.6e-3 over the first two steps (fp8 rollout, bf16 train, within the GLM LoRA cookbook's documented fp8-rollout range).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Sync time in the table above. No change on the forward path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -193,11 +193,12 @@ def send_weights_to_remote_instance(
     def deserialize_own_rank(self, serialized_named_tensors):
         """Each rank deserializes only its own payload (index tp_rank);
         deserializing another rank's copy would break producer-side CUDA-IPC
-        refcounting."""
+        refcounting. A single entry is one payload shared by every rank: HTTP
+        callers ship plain CPU tensors, which carry no per-rank IPC handles, so
+        they need not send a copy per rank."""
         monkey_patch_torch_reductions()
-        return MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize(
-            serialized_named_tensors[get_parallel().tp_rank]
-        )
+        index = get_parallel().tp_rank if len(serialized_named_tensors) > 1 else 0
+        return MultiprocessingSerializer.deserialize(serialized_named_tensors[index])
 
     def get_weights_by_name(self, recv_req: GetWeightsByNameReqInput):
         parameter = self.model_runner.weight_exporter.get_weights_by_name(

@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+"""A tensor weight update reads its own rank's payload, or one payload shared by every rank."""
+
+import io
+import pickle
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.tp_worker import BaseTpWorker
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _payload(value: float) -> bytes:
+    # HTTP callers ship a plain pickle of CPU tensors (no shared-memory or IPC handles).
+    buffer = io.BytesIO()
+    pickle.dump([("weight", torch.full((2, 2), value))], buffer)
+    return buffer.getvalue()
+
+
+class TestDeserializeOwnRank(unittest.TestCase):
+    def _read(self, serialized, tp_rank: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # The torch-reduction monkey patch is process-wide; a plain pickle of CPU tensors
+        # does not need it, so keep it out of other tests in the same process.
+        with (
+            patch("sglang.srt.managers.tp_worker.monkey_patch_torch_reductions"),
+            get_parallel().override(tp_rank=tp_rank),
+        ):
+            ((name, tensor),) = BaseTpWorker.deserialize_own_rank(None, serialized)
+        self.assertEqual(name, "weight")
+        return tensor
+
+    def test_per_rank_list_reads_own_entry(self):
+        serialized = [_payload(float(rank)) for rank in range(4)]
+        for rank in range(4):
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(
+                    self._read(serialized, rank), torch.full((2, 2), float(rank))
+                )
+            )
+
+    def test_single_entry_is_shared_by_every_rank(self):
+        serialized = [_payload(7.0)]
+        for rank in range(4):
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(self._read(serialized, rank), torch.full((2, 2), 7.0))
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
